key_insight: Semantic early-stopping can replace fixed iteration caps in LLM agent loops by halting when draft meaning and measured quality stop improving, saving tokens without hurting answer quality.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent workflows like Writer–Critic loops, this offers a practical control policy that improves token efficiency and exposes when extra iterations are no longer worth their cost.
method: Track cosine distance between consecutive draft embeddings with a patience window.
Optionally gate stopping on stagnating quality judged across rounds.
Replay all stopping policies on the same generated trajectories with cached judge calls for fair comparison.
evidence_signal: On 60 HotpotQA test questions, the judge-free semantic stopper cut operational tokens by 38% versus max_iterations at parity quality, while the oracle-best round was still substantially better than any practical policy.
watch_item: The full quality-gated version can be more expensive than it saves because per-round LLM judging dominates runtime and token cost.
paper_title: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
